title: Clarify OpenAI-compat tool call semantics: decision-encoding header, selection markers, and stream framing
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Clarifies OpenAI-compat tool call signaling: adds decision-encoding header and selection markers; improves streaming framing for tool messages to reduce ambiguity. Backwards compatible toggle preserved.
description:
Motivation: Users integrating OpenAI-style function/tool calling reported ambiguous tool selection signals in streaming responses and differing schema encodings across upstream SDKs. This PR standardizes a metadata-first compatibility layer to: (1) encode the selected tool decision explicitly (no token-level encodings), (2) mark choice boundaries in streams so consumers can reliably reassemble tool invocation messages, and (3) preserve backwards compatibility via a feature flag for legacy tool_choice consumers.

What changed (high level):
- Introduce an immutable response header 'x-rw-tool-decision' with a compact decision encoding (json-compact, base64 when streaming) that contains: tool_id, decision_rank, schema_fingerprint. This avoids embedding selection hints into text tokens.
- Add selection markers in streaming payloads: a lightweight marker <<rw-choice:IDX>> is emitted as a separate framed event (not interleaved tokens) to indicate which tool index was chosen; the marker is emitted prior to the tool message frame.
- Stream framing changes: introduce frame types 'assistant', 'tool-invoke-meta', and 'tool-output' so consumers can distinguish meta vs payload without heuristic parsing. Frames are emitted as small JSON envelopes over the existing SSE/WS stream.
- Schema fingerprinting: compute sha1 hex of canonicalized tool JSON schema and include fingerprint in decision header. This supports robust mapping between requested schema and served tool signature.
- Backwards-compat toggle: if the client sets Accept: application/openai-legacy-toolchoice, the runtime will emit a v1 compatibility event 'tool_choice' (legacy payload) in addition to the new headers/frames for a period of time.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for decision header encoding and integration tests for streaming reassembly; docs page updated with examples (python/ts) showing how to consume the new frames.

Checklist: 
- [x] Decision header encoder/decoder implemented (runtime + API gateway)
- [x] Stream frame types implemented and integrated into the SSE/WS fanout
- [x] Schema fingerprint validator added to model registry mapping step
- [x] Backwards compat flag and E2E regression tests
- [x] Docs + migration notes

Commits summary: 
- feat(compat): add x-rw-tool-decision header encoder (maya)
- feat(stream): introduce frame types and marker emission in sse broker (oliver)
- feat(registry): schema fingerprinting and validator (sofia)
- test: add streaming reassembly e2e (ethan)
- docs: compat migration + examples (maya)

Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/proxy/response_headers.go -- add encoder for tool decision header and tests
- runtime/stream/broker.go -- implement frame types, marker emission, and consumer API
- api/compat/openai_mapper.go -- map legacy tool_choice to new header+frames when flag set
- registry/schema/signer.go -- canonicalize schema and produce sha1 fingerprint
- examples/openai/stream-consumer.py -- sample consumer that handles the new frames
- docs/openai-compat/tool-calls.md -- migration guide and examples
- integration-tests/compat/stream_tool_reassembly_test.go -- e2e test harness

Small illustrative snippet (runtime header encoder):
from: "x-rw-tool-decision: {\"tool_id\":\"translate_v2\",\"rank\":0,\"schema_fp\":\"6a1f4c2d...\" }"

Review thread (high level): 
- Oliver: "Prefer header vs embedding in tokens; what's the size cost for headers on large batch responses?"
- Maya (reply): "Header is ~200 bytes worst-case; we already carry several metadata headers; added a bench showing <0.5% impact on 1k QPS baseline."
- Sofia: "Schema fingerprinting supports detecting model mismatch; ensure we can fallback when fingerprint doesn't match stored registry."
- Maya: "Implemented fallback: if mismatch and Accept includes legacy, we emit legacy tool_choice and log a telemetry event for manual triage."
- Ethan: "Integration test flakes on CI when repeated SSE disconnects occur."
- Maya: "Added retry on broker reconnect and hardened test harness to use deterministic jitter; reran CI."

CI and perf: All CI passed on final run (unit/integration/lint). Microbenchmarks: decision header adds 0.4% p99 overhead in median path; streaming reassembly latency improved slightly due to explicit framing avoiding heuristic parsing.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after approvals. No behavioural breaking-change for clients that do not opt into the new Accept header; default path is new header+frames. Deprecated legacy 'tool_choice' will be removed after 90-day migration window; docs contain migration steps and example consumers.

Backport: Not required. Monitoring/telemetry: added 'compat.decision.fallback' counter and a dashboard tile documenting fingerprint mismatches and legacy-toggle usage.
